![Research paper thumbnail of Sustaining the Malaysian Environment through Litter Reduction: A Maqasidi Approach](https://a.academia-assets.com/images/blank-paper.jpg)

Sustaining the Malaysian Environment through Litter Reduction: A Maqasidi Approach

Since the introduction of the Environmental Quality Act (1974), Malaysian law has recognised the ... more Since the introduction of the Environmental Quality Act (1974), Malaysian law has recognised the need to protect the environment from pollutants and excess waste. However, the general population has yet to collaborate with these prescriptions at the most fundamental level, as the obvious and overwhelming amount of littering might function as evidence of an essential aspect of Malaysian culture to be apathetic towards environmental hygiene. Although the government has attempted to curb this unhealthy behaviour through educational initiatives, increased awareness through marketing campaigns, and selected law enforcement patrolling, it is still considered a major problem in the country. Despite the fact that the majority of the nation follows the religion of Islam, many Muslims do not consider environmental hygiene to be an essential aspect of their religion or culture – nor does the government who represents the majority see fit to instil more aggressive policies towards this ailment. This paper addresses current Malaysian legislation and enforcement in the context of personal pollution (littering) through a maqasdi approach, highlighting the basic principles in Islam associated with environmental management and societal benefit. Simultaneously, it recognizes that a strictly ‘awareness approach’ is insufficient. In conclusion, this paper argues for the precedence of a holistic implementation of litter reduction across the nation through more effective educational programs, harsher punishments, and more efficient methods of environmental management through law enforcement.

61 Views

![Research paper thumbnail of Still Colonized? Liberalism in Muslim Thought](https://a.academia-assets.com/images/blank-paper.jpg)

Still Colonized? Liberalism in Muslim Thought

This lecture focusses on the long-entrenched ideals of Liberalism within Muslim politics and beli... more This lecture focusses on the long-entrenched ideals of Liberalism within Muslim politics and beliefs over the past few centuries prior to and post colonialism. Rather than being a historical survey, a deeper analysis and deconstruction of this hybrid variation of Islam shall be attempted, including a thorough elucidation of the concepts of ‘empowerment’ and ‘disenfranchisement’ – the primary subjects of this conference. This lecture argues that the major effects of Liberalism within Muslim thought have been the destruction of the Muslim identity and religious tradition through the addition of values alien to Islam. These trends have manifested themselves in two distinct ways: (1) Influence and control of Muslim majority states by foreign powers through economic and military means and (2) widespread political and societal chaos through terrorism and interstate violence. Both the concepts of ‘empowerment’ and ‘disenfranchisement’ within the Liberalists construct have been the primary influences behind these problems, naturally affecting other members of Muslim societies as well, such as women. Prior to sowing the seeds of ‘empowerment’ among Muslimah and Muslims at large, we need to first find the fertile soil that Liberalism has denigrated and made impotent; Islam without Liberalism.
